scope: VICH guideline on residual solvents in veterinary medicinal products, active substances and excipients, cited by FEEDAP 2017 (5023) section 2.1.4 for residual solvents in feed additives. It is written for veterinary medicinal products; the 10 g/day basis of Option 1 should be checked against the feed additive's daily intake. Per-solvent limits are in vich_gl18r2_solvents.json. Grounds the assistant and the residual-solvent comparison.

guidance.title: VICH GL18(R2) Impurities: residual solvents in new veterinary medicinal products, active substances and excipients (revision 2)
guidance.author: VICH / EMA CVMP
guidance.citation: VICH, 2023. Revised Guideline 18 - Impurities: residual solvents in new veterinary medicinal products, active substances and excipients (Revision 2). EMA/CVMP/VICH/502/1999, adopted by CVMP 17 May 2023, in effect April 2024.

entries.title: Three solvent classes
entries.requirement: Class 1 (Table 1): avoid, unless strongly justified in a risk-benefit assessment. Class 2 (Table 2): limit. Class 3 (Table 3): less toxic, preferred. The lists are not exhaustive and limits may change as safety data appear.
entries.quote: Some solvents that are known to cause unacceptable toxicities (Class 1, Table 1) should be avoided in the production of active substances, excipients, or veterinary medicinal products unless their use can be strongly justified in a risk-benefit assessment [...] The lists are not exhaustive and other solvents can be used and later added to the lists
guidance_anchors: Some solvents that are known to cause unacceptable toxicities (Class 1, Table 1) should be avoided in the production of active substances, excipients, or veterinary medicinal products unless their use can be strongly justified in a risk-benefit assessment
The lists are not exhaustive and other solvents can be used and later added to the lists

entries.title: Purpose and what it does not cover
entries.requirement: Recommends acceptable amounts of residual solvents for the safety of the target animal and of residues in products from food-producing animals. It does not address solvents deliberately used as excipients, nor solvates, but their content should be evaluated and justified.
entries.quote: The objective of this guideline is to recommend acceptable amounts for residual solvents in pharmaceuticals for the safety of the target animal as well as for the safety of residues in products derived from treated food producing animals [...] This guideline does not address solvents deliberately used as excipients nor does it address solvates
guidance_anchors: The objective of this guideline is to recommend acceptable amounts for residual solvents in pharmaceuticals for the safety of the target animal as well as for the safety of residues in products derived from treated food producing animals
This guideline does not address solvents deliberately used as excipients nor does it address solvates

entries.title: When to test
entries.requirement: Test for residual solvents when production or purification is known to leave them, and only for solvents used or produced in manufacture or purification. A cumulative calculation from the ingredients can replace testing of the product if it comes out at or below the recommended level.
entries.quote: testing should be performed for residual solvents when production or purification processes are known to result in the presence of such solvents [...] It is only necessary to test for solvents that are used or produced in the manufacture or purification of medicinal substances, excipients, or veterinary medicinal products
guidance_anchors: testing should be performed for residual solvents when production or purification processes are known to result in the presence of such solvents
It is only necessary to test for solvents that are used or produced in the manufacture or purification of medicinal substances, excipients, or veterinary medicinal products

entries.title: Class definitions and PDE
entries.requirement: Class 1: known or strongly suspected human carcinogens and environmental hazards. Class 2: non-genotoxic animal carcinogens or agents of other irreversible toxicity (neurotoxicity, teratogenicity), or suspected of other significant reversible toxicity. Class 3: low toxic potential, PDE of 50 mg/day or more. PDE = permitted daily exposure.
entries.quote: Known human carcinogens, strongly suspected human carcinogens, and environmental hazards [...] Class 3 solvents have PDEs of 50 mg or more per day
guidance_anchors: Known human carcinogens, strongly suspected human carcinogens, and environmental hazards
Class 3 solvents have PDEs of 50 mg or more per day

entries.title: Class 2 Option 1: concentration limits
entries.requirement: Use the ppm limits of Table 2, calculated as 1000 x PDE (mg/day) / dose (g/day) for a 10 g daily product mass. Acceptable for any component if the daily dose is unknown or fixed; if all components meet them they can be used in any proportion. Products dosed above 10 g/day go to Option 2.
entries.quote: The concentration limits in ppm stated in Table 2 can be used. They were calculated using equation (1) below by assuming a product mass of 10 g administered daily [...] Products that are administered in doses greater than 10 g per day should be considered under Option 2
guidance_anchors: The concentration limits in ppm stated in Table 2 can be used. They were calculated using equation (1) below by assuming a product mass of 10 g administered daily
Products that are administered in doses greater than 10 g per day should be considered under Option 2

entries.title: Class 2 Option 2: PDE with the known maximum daily dose
entries.requirement: Use the PDE in mg/day with the known maximum daily dose to set the allowed concentration, provided the solvent has been reduced to the practical minimum and limits are realistic for analytical precision and manufacturing. Amounts in all components can be summed; the daily sum must stay below the PDE.
entries.quote: The sum of the amounts of solvent per day should be less than that given by the PDE [...] The limits should be realistic in relation to analytical precision, manufacturing capability, reasonable variation in the manufacturing process
guidance_anchors: The sum of the amounts of solvent per day should be less than that given by the PDE
The limits should be realistic in relation to analytical precision, manufacturing capability, reasonable variation in the manufacturing process

entries.title: Class 2 Option 3: higher justified limits
entries.requirement: Applicants may justify higher limits from the actual daily dose, actual target species and toxicological data, with consumer safety considered. Handled case by case by the authorities.
entries.quote: Applicants may justify higher levels for the PDE and concentration limit based upon the actual daily dose, actual target species, and relevant toxicological data and considering consumer safety aspects [...] Use of Option 3 will be handled on a case by case basis by the regulatory authorities
guidance_anchors: Applicants may justify higher levels for the PDE and concentration limit based upon the actual daily dose, actual target species, and relevant toxicological data and considering consumer safety aspects
Use of Option 3 will be handled on a case by case basis by the regulatory authorities

entries.title: Analytical procedures
entries.requirement: Typically gas chromatography; use harmonised pharmacopoeial procedures if feasible, otherwise a validated method. If only Class 3 solvents are present, a non-specific method such as loss on drying may be used.
entries.quote: Residual solvents are typically determined using chromatographic techniques such as gas chromatography [...] If only Class 3 solvents are present, a non-specific method such as loss on drying may be used
guidance_anchors: Residual solvents are typically determined using chromatographic techniques such as gas chromatography
If only Class 3 solvents are present, a non-specific method such as loss on drying may be used

entries.title: Reporting residual solvent levels
entries.requirement: Suppliers can state that only Class 3 solvents are likely (loss on drying < 0.5%), or name the Class 2 solvents and confirm they are below the Option 1 limit. Class 1 solvents likely to be present must be identified and quantified, as must Class 2 or 3 solvents above their Option 1 limit or 0.5%. 'Likely' covers the last step's solvent and earlier solvents not consistently removed.
entries.quote: If Class 1 solvents are likely to be present, they should be identified and quantified [...] If solvents of Class 2 or Class 3 are present at greater than their Option 1 limits or 0.5%, respectively, they should be identified and quantified
guidance_anchors: If Class 1 solvents are likely to be present, they should be identified and quantified
If solvents of Class 2 or Class 3 are present at greater than their Option 1 limits or 0.5%, respectively, they should be identified and quantified

entries.title: Class 1 limits (Table 1)
entries.requirement: If unavoidable for a significant therapeutic advance, restrict to: benzene 2 ppm, carbon tetrachloride 4 ppm, 1,2-dichloroethane 5 ppm, 1,1-dichloroethene 8 ppm, 1,1,1-trichloroethane 1500 ppm.
entries.quote: Solvents in Class 1 should not be employed in the manufacture of active substances, excipients, and veterinary medicinal products because of their unacceptable toxicity or their deleterious environmental effect [...] Benzene 2 Carcinogen
guidance_anchors: Solvents in Class 1 should not be employed in the manufacture of active substances, excipients, and veterinary medicinal products because of their unacceptable toxicity or their deleterious environmental effect
Benzene 2 Carcinogen

entries.title: Class 2 limits (Table 2)
entries.requirement: Class 2 solvents are limited for inherent toxicity; PDEs are given to 0.1 mg/day and concentrations to the nearest 10 ppm, which do not reflect the analytical precision needed. See the structured table for each solvent.
entries.quote: Solvents in Table 2 should be limited in pharmaceutical products because of their inherent toxicity [...] Acetonitrile 4.1 410
guidance_anchors: Solvents in Table 2 should be limited in pharmaceutical products because of their inherent toxicity
Acetonitrile 4.1 410

entries.title: Class 3 solvents
entries.requirement: Low toxic potential; 50 mg/day or less (5000 ppm or 0.5% under Option 1) is acceptable without justification; higher amounts may be acceptable if realistic for manufacturing capability and GMP.
entries.quote: amounts of these residual solvents of 50 mg per day or less (corresponding to 5000 ppm or 0.5% under Option 1) would be acceptable without justification
guidance_anchors: amounts of these residual solvents of 50 mg per day or less (corresponding to 5000 ppm or 0.5% under Option 1) would be acceptable without justification

entries.title: Solvents without a PDE (Table 4)
entries.requirement: For solvents lacking adequate toxicological data (e.g. isooctane, isopropyl ether, petroleum ether, trifluoroacetic acid) the manufacturer must justify the residual levels.
entries.quote: Manufacturers should supply justification for residual levels of these and other solvents for which a PDE has not been established for use in pharmaceutical products
guidance_anchors: Manufacturers should supply justification for residual levels of these and other solvents for which a PDE has not been established for use in pharmaceutical products
